questions.answer: I do, generally. Having a rough plan gives me direction and stops me wasting time. That said, I try not to over-plan, because some of the best moments come from being a little [[spontaneous]].

questions.q: Do you usually plan your weekends?
questions.answer: Loosely. I'll usually have one or two things in mind, like visiting relatives or catching up on reading, but I leave plenty of room for rest. After a busy week, a [[laid-back]] weekend is exactly what I need.

questions.q: Are you good at making decisions?
questions.answer: I'd say I'm decisive with small things, but I take my time over big ones, weighing up the options carefully. Occasionally I [[deliberate]] for too long, but I'd rather be thorough than rush and regret it.

questions.q: Who do you ask for advice when you have an important decision to make?
questions.answer: Usually my father. He ran his own business for over thirty years, so he has a very practical, [[level-headed]] way of looking at things. For more personal matters, though, I often talk to my elder sister.

questions.q: Is it better to plan for the future or live in the moment?
questions.answer: I think you need a balance. Planning ahead gives you security, especially with things like careers and savings. But if you're [[fixated on]] the future all the time, you can easily miss the joy of what's happening right now.
